arms.predicted: Exhaustive sweep of 900 reduced-space configs will produce Pareto density 8-25% (72-225 non-dominated), spanning at least 4 GPU-count tiers with genuine within-tier tradeoffs.
arms.observed: 900/900 configs evaluated in 68.8s. Pareto front: 238/900 = 26.4% density. Exhaustive reference HV = 5.2962e+10. Pareto front spans 4 GPU tiers (gpu_count 1,2,4,8). Within-tier tradeoffs confirmed: kv_blocks cliff interaction and batch scheduling bottleneck create distinct Pareto points per tier.
arms.diagnostic_note: Density 26.4% is just above the predicted 8-25% range. Slight over-prediction likely from batch={128,256,512} being less redundant than expected. Qualitative prediction (non-trivial search difficulty, multi-tier coverage) is confirmed.

arms.predicted: NSGA-II on reduced space reaches 95% of exhaustive HV at least 80 evaluations before random. At eval=80: NSGA-II >= 93%, random <= 88%. Convergence gap larger than iter-3's 40-eval gap.
arms.observed: NSGA-II reaches 95% of exhaustive HV (5.2962e+10) at eval=117 (interpolated). Random reaches 95% at eval=164 (interpolated). Gap: 47 evals. At eval=80: NSGA-II=91.2% (predicted >=93%), random=88.6% (predicted <=88%). Convergence trajectory: eval=40: 84.7%, 80: 91.2%, 120: 95.3%, 160: 96.5%, 200: 97.8%. Final HV=5.1804e+10 (97.8% of exhaustive). Pareto front: 96 solutions at eval=200.
arms.diagnostic_note: Directional effect confirmed: NSGA-II converges faster than random (47-eval gap vs iter-3's 40-eval gap). Gap DID increase with reduced space. However, gap is 47 evals, not 80 as predicted. At eval=80, NSGA-II was 91.2% not >=93%. Reduced space 22% coverage (200/900) and 26.4% Pareto density allow random to cover adequate Pareto front faster than predicted, capping the gap.

arms.predicted: Random search reaches 95% of exhaustive HV at eval=160 or later. Final HV within 3% of exhaustive but below NSGA-II's final.
arms.observed: Random reaches 95% of exhaustive at eval=164 (interpolated). Convergence: eval=40: 84.7%, 80: 88.6%, 120: 91.0%, 160: 94.9%, 200: 96.1%. Final HV=5.0873e+10 (96.1% of exhaustive). NSGA-II final (97.8%) exceeds random final (96.1%). At eval=40, random and NSGA-II have identical HV (4.4873e+10), confirming uniform initialization diverges only after evolution.
arms.diagnostic_note: Random reaches 95% at eval=164 (>160 as predicted). Final HV is 3.9% below exhaustive (slightly outside 'within 3%' prediction but qualitatively accurate). Identical HV at eval=40 between NSGA-II and random confirms both start from same uniform random point.

arms.predicted: NSGA-II full space reaches 95% of its own final HV at eval=120. Full-space NSGA-II converges to its ceiling slower than reduced-space NSGA-II converges to exhaustive.
arms.observed: NSGA-II full reaches 95% of its own ceiling (5.8494e+10) at eval=71 — FASTER than predicted eval=120. More critically: full-space NSGA-II HV EXCEEDS the reduced-space exhaustive Pareto front (5.6611e+10 at eval=80 = 106.9% of reduced exhaustive). Root cause: block_size=32 (assumed non-differentiating) is HIGHLY differentiating for tp=8. At tp=8,inst=1,batch=512,kv=3000: block_size=16 -> rps=21.35, ttft_p99=2323ms, 107 preemptions; block_size=32 -> rps=26.28, ttft_p99=25ms, 0 preemptions. block_size doubles effective KV token capacity (3000 x 32=96k vs 3000 x 16=48k tokens), eliminating preemptions entirely for this GPU tier.
arms.diagnostic_note: Secondary criterion refuted: full-space NSGA-II converges to a higher ceiling faster than reduced-space NSGA-II. The assumption that block_size_in_tokens is non-differentiating was incorrect for high-TP configurations. total_kv_blocks specifies block COUNT, not tokens; block_size multiplies the effective token capacity. Fixing block_size=16 in the reduced space inadvertently constrained tp=8 configs below their stress-free threshold (48k vs 96k tokens at kv=3000).

discrepancy_analysis: Primary finding: block_size_in_tokens is NOT non-differentiating for high-TP configs. It multiplies effective KV token capacity (blocks x block_size), creating a dramatic qualitative transition at tp=8 (107 preemptions -> 0, ttft 2323ms -> 25ms with block_size 16->32 at kv=3000). This was missed in earlier probing because probing focused on tp=2,inst=2 where KV stress patterns differ. The convergence speed gap for NSGA-II vs random on reduced space increased from ~40 evals (iter-3) to ~47 evals (iter-4), confirming the crossover efficiency mechanism but at smaller magnitude than predicted. The high Pareto density (26.4%) and 22% budget-to-space coverage ratio limit the maximum achievable gap at budget=200.
